input.strategy_title: FIPS 140-3 compliance for the model serving stack
input.strategy_markdown:
## Problem Statement

Public-sector deals require the model serving stack to run on FIPS-enabled
OpenShift clusters using validated cryptographic modules. Today KServe
components and the serving data plane link non-validated crypto libraries in
several images, and we have no compliance evidence package. Certification
involves an external accredited laboratory (historical turnaround: six to nine
months) and mandatory security review board sign-off at defined milestones —
these human and third-party gates dominate the schedule regardless of
engineering speed.

## High-Level Requirements

| ID | Priority | Requirement |
|-------|----------|-------------|
| HLR-1 | P0 | All serving-stack images run correctly on FIPS-enabled clusters using validated crypto modules (no non-validated crypto in the request path). |
| HLR-2 | P0 | A compliance evidence package (module inventory, build attestations, test results) is assembled and submitted through the security review board to the external certification lab. |
| HLR-3 | P1 | CI enforces FIPS regressions: a gating check fails any serving-stack build that reintroduces non-validated crypto usage. |
| HLR-4 | P2 | Documentation states the FIPS support posture and cluster prerequisites. |

## Affected Components

- KServe
- Platform Operator

## Out of Scope

- FIPS posture for workbenches, pipelines, and training (separate strategies)
- Common Criteria certification

## Open Questions

None on scope — but note that lab scheduling and review-board cadence are
externally controlled and cannot be compressed by engineering effort.

# FIPS crypto usage audit and remediation-path investigation for serving-stack images

## Description

This investigation resolves the central unknown of the FIPS 140-3 compliance
effort for the model serving stack: which serving-stack images — the KServe
component images and the Platform Operator image — link non-validated
cryptographic libraries, and what the validated-crypto remediation path is for
each finding. Its deliverable is a complete module inventory (the seed of the
compliance evidence package) and a per-image remediation plan that the
remediation work for each component builds on. The remediation direction is
fixed by the strategy (remove non-validated crypto from the request path), but
which images, which libraries, and which replacements apply is not yet known —
the answer changes what the downstream remediation work does.

## Scope

- Enumerate every serving-stack image in scope: all KServe component images
  and the Platform Operator image.
- For each image, identify the cryptographic libraries and modules linked
  into it (base images, language runtimes, vendored dependencies) and classify
  each as validated or non-validated for FIPS 140-3 purposes.
- Determine a remediation path for every non-validated finding: validated
  replacement library or base image, dependency upgrade, or rebuild with
  FIPS-appropriate build configuration.
- Identify findings whose remediation requires changes in upstream projects
  (dependency releases, upstream patches), including what the upstream change
  is and who owns it.
- Produce the module inventory and per-image remediation plan as a reviewable
  artifact, handed to the per-component remediation work.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A module inventory exists that covers every in-scope serving-stack image
  and lists, per image, the linked crypto modules with their
  validated/non-validated classification — a image omitted from the inventory
  is a failure.
- Every non-validated finding in the inventory has an identified remediation
  path naming the validated replacement (library, base image, or build
  configuration change).
- Findings requiring upstream changes are listed with the upstream project,
  the change needed, and whether a midstream workaround exists.
- The remediation plan is handed off to the per-component remediation work
  with per-image actions such that each component team can start without
  re-deriving the analysis.

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-1 (P0)** — enables: the audit determines which images must be
  remediated and how; the remediation epics for KServe and the Platform
  Operator are gated on this outcome.
- **HLR-2 (P0)** — partial: the module inventory produced here is a required
  input of the compliance evidence package.

# FIPS 140-3 validated-crypto remediation for KServe serving-stack images

## Description

This epic makes every KServe serving-stack image run correctly on FIPS-enabled
OpenShift clusters using validated cryptographic modules, with no non-validated
crypto in the serving request path, and wires a gating FIPS regression check
into the KServe build pipeline so any build that reintroduces non-validated
crypto usage fails. It applies the per-image remediation plan produced by the
FIPS crypto audit to the KServe component images.

## Scope

- Apply the audit's remediation plan to all KServe component images: swap
  non-validated crypto libraries and base images for validated ones, upgrade
  or rebuild dependencies, and adjust build configuration as the plan
  specifies, removing non-validated crypto from the request path.
- Update the module inventory entries for every remediated KServe image so
  the compliance evidence package reflects the post-remediation state.
- Add a gating FIPS regression check to the KServe build pipeline that fails
  any KServe build reintroducing non-validated crypto usage (this epic owns
  the enforcement for the KServe image surfaces it converts).
- Validate the remediated images on a FIPS-enabled OpenShift cluster:
  InferenceServices deploy and serve requests correctly in both serverless
  and raw deployment modes, with the request path using validated crypto.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Every KServe serving-stack image contains no non-validated crypto in the
  request path, verified by re-running the audit's scanning method on the
  remediated images.
- Remediated KServe images deploy InferenceServices and serve inference
  requests correctly on a FIPS-enabled OpenShift cluster, in both serverless
  and raw deployment modes.
- The KServe build pipeline carries a gating FIPS check that fails a build
  which reintroduces non-validated crypto usage and passes the remediated
  builds (build pipeline green with the check in place).
- The module inventory is updated to reflect the post-remediation state of
  every KServe image.

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-1 (P0)** — primary: all serving-stack images run correctly on
  FIPS-enabled clusters using validated crypto modules (KServe images).
- **HLR-3 (P1)** — bundled: the gating FIPS regression check for KServe
  builds is carried in this epic rather than a standalone enforcement epic
  because it guards the exact build surfaces this epic converts and shares
  its detection tooling and pipeline wiring — it is not separately
  schedulable from the remediation of the same surfaces.

## Risks / Notes

- Remediation actions depend on the FIPS crypto audit's findings; if a
  finding requires an upstream dependency release that is not yet available,
  the remediation approach for that image is rewritten accordingly.
- Security review board sign-off at defined milestones is a mandatory human
  gate on the compliance program.

# FIPS 140-3 compliance evidence package assembly and submission

## Description

This epic assembles the FIPS 140-3 compliance evidence package for the model
serving stack — module inventory, build attestations, and test results — and
submits it through the security review board to the external accredited
certification lab. The strategy currently has no compliance evidence package;
this epic produces it from the outputs of the serving-stack FIPS remediation
and hands it off to the certification process.

## Scope

- Assemble the final module inventory from the FIPS crypto audit and the
  post-remediation inventory updates for the KServe images and the Platform
  Operator image.
- Collect build attestations for every remediated serving-stack image from
  its build pipeline.
- Collect the FIPS-enabled cluster validation test results for the
  remediated KServe images and the Platform Operator image.
- Compose the package to the certification lab's submission requirements
  (inventory, attestations, test results, and supporting documentation).
- Submit the package through the security review board and hand it off to
  the external certification lab; track it through the submission
  milestone.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The evidence package contains the complete module inventory, build
  attestations for every remediated serving-stack image, and the
  FIPS-enabled cluster test results for the serving stack.
- The package passes an internal completeness review against the
  certification lab's submission requirements before hand-off (every
  required element present; a missing element is a failure).
- The package is submitted through the security review board and handed off
  to the external certification lab, with the submission recorded and
  tracked.

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-2 (P0)** — primary: the compliance evidence package (module
  inventory, build attestations, test results) is assembled and submitted
  through the security review board to the external certification lab.

## Risks / Notes

- Certification lab turnaround is historically six to nine months and the
  security review board meets on a fixed cadence; both are externally
  controlled and cannot be compressed by engineering effort. They are
  schedule risks on this epic, not acceptance criteria — this epic's
  engineering completion point is the assembled, internally validated, and
  submitted package.
- Certification outcome (lab approval) is beyond this strategy's HLR-2
  completion point (submission) and is tracked as a program risk.

# FIPS support posture and cluster prerequisites documentation

## Description

This epic documents the FIPS 140-3 support posture of the model serving stack
and the cluster prerequisites for running it on FIPS-enabled OpenShift
clusters, reflecting the remediated state of the serving-stack images. It runs
last so the documentation describes what was actually built and submitted.

## Scope

Content outline:

- FIPS support posture of the model serving stack: what is supported after
  remediation, which images use validated cryptographic modules, and any
  remaining limitations (out-of-scope areas: workbenches, pipelines,
  training; Common Criteria is out of scope entirely).
- Cluster prerequisites: FIPS-enabled OpenShift clusters, validated crypto
  module requirements, and any installation or configuration constraints
  (including deployment-mode considerations for the serving stack).
- Guidance for public-sector and regulated deployments on verifying the
  FIPS posture, referencing the compliance evidence package submitted to
  the certification lab.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Published documentation states the FIPS support posture of the model
  serving stack and the cluster prerequisites for FIPS-enabled clusters.
- The documentation is technically reviewed against the implemented
  remediation (postures, images, and prerequisites match what was built and
  submitted) and revised until review passes.
- The documentation is accurate against the platform architecture context
  for the serving stack (deployment modes and dependencies as documented
  there).

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-4 (P2)** — primary: documentation states the FIPS support posture
  and cluster prerequisites.

Full decomposition (not triaged): the strategy spans two components (KServe,
Platform Operator), multiple teams, and multiple work streams (image
remediation, CI enforcement, compliance evidence assembly and submission,
documentation), so neither the below-threshold nor the docs-only triage path
applies.
